clue.text: Part-time secretary brought in by attorney for trial

indicators.note: something brought in by another is taken inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: ATT is a standard abbreviation for attorney
a temp is a temporary office worker, often a secretary

explanation.surface: A temporary secretary is hired by a lawyer to help with a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' reads as a court case beside the attorney, but it means an effort or try.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a test or try, the same as an effort made at something.

clue.text: Agile figure: a feline, going about to plunder

indicators.note: going about means surrounding, so the word for the animal wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a cat is a feline
to plunder is to rob

explanation.surface: A nimble cat circles round to steal something.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat is a performer known for agile gymnastic feats.

clue.text: Circus performer not accustomed to slack?

definitions.text: Circus performer not accustomed to slack?

parts.words: Circus performer not accustomed to slack?
parts.note: a performer who walks a taut line high up is never used to a slack one, with a pun on slack meaning idleness

explanation.surface: A circus artist who never gets any slack.
explanation.definitionFit: This performer balances on a taut high wire, so slackness is literally unknown to them.

clue.text: Bloke not fully accepting United's attack

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the shortened word holds the abbreviation
not fully means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a bloke is a male, a man
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A man partly takes in a football club's attack.
explanation.walkthrough: MALE loses its E to give MAL, which takes in U.
explanation.definitionFit: To maul is to savage or attack violently.

clue.text: Excellent but its downhill to the clubhouse from here

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned British slang word for first-rate

definitions.text: its downhill to the clubhouse from here
definitions.meaning: literally the highest hole on a golf course, from where the walk back is downhill

explanation.surface: A golfer delighted at reaching a point from which the clubhouse is all downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for first-rate, and literally the highest hole on a golf course.

clue.text: Cut tip of corn and jumped

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its leading letter, so only the opening letter of corn is used

parts.note: to jump is to hop, so jumped gives hopped

explanation.surface: Someone cut the top off an ear of corn and leapt about.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopped means cut into pieces with a blade, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Shot almost on target? go out in tournament

annotationWithheld.why: Shot almost on target? go out in tournament (5-2): CLOSE (almost on target) fits, but nothing in 'go out in tournament' gives UP; likely OCR loss or a misprint
annotationWithheld.clue: Shot almost on target? go out in tournament

clue.text: Golf tournament: in here everyone's invited?

definitions.text: Golf tournament: in here everyone's invited?

parts.words: Golf tournament: in here everyone's invited?
parts.note: the famous golf championship lets any qualifier enter, and a home where every guest is welcome likewise admits all comers

explanation.surface: A golf event at a venue where everyone is welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: An open house is a home or event where all visitors are welcome.

clue.text: Solicit contributions for visa covering Panama?

parts.note: a pass is a permit, like a visa
round means around, covering something on all sides
a Panama is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about getting a visa that also covers Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' looks like the country needing a visa, but it is the straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing round a hat is the traditional way of collecting money from a group.

clue.text: Bad rule needs reforming to become long-lasting

indicators.note: reforming means forming again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unjust rule must be changed before it can last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something durable lasts a long time without wearing out.

clue.text: Academic forges superior's working

indicators.note: working suggests letters set in motion and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone forges their boss's signature while the boss is at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' looks like part of the story of forgery, but it signals that the letters of FORGES SUPERIORS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A Regius chair is a royal professorship at an old British university, so its holder is a senior academic.

clue.text: Item for washers at the bowl, possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints that the words could be arranged another way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something used by washers at the basin, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' tells you to rearrange the letters of AT THE BOWL; the phrase also fits the surface of someone washing at a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: People who wash dry themselves with a large cloth meant for drying after bathing.

clue.text: See 10
Marine creature, caught on sandy ridge, turning

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: turning means the word for the sandy ridge is read backwards

parts.note: a bar is a ridge of sand in a river mouth or near a coast

explanation.surface: A sea creature is captured on a sandbank as it turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab is a shelled sea animal, a kind of crustacean.

clue.text: Fellow actor going to modern art centre in Central American country

parts.note: a co-star acts alongside another lead
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London

explanation.surface: An actor's colleague heads to a gallery in Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a country in Central America between Nicaragua and Panama.

clue.text: See 6
Pair working in fields, as recalled in book

indicators.note: in places the reversed farming word inside the word for a book

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: recalled, read as called back, means the farming word is read backwards

parts.note: a farmer working in fields might sow seed

explanation.surface: Two people working the fields, as remembered in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working in fields' is a clue to a farm job, read as a verb; 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a couple or duo, two people together.

clue.text: Favouring electrical safety device in effusive style

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a fuse breaks a circuit when the current gets too high

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses gushingly about the merits of a fuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Profuse means lavish or overflowing, as effusive praise or thanks would be.

clue.text: Good humour seen around street in city

indicators.note: one piece seen around another wraps it, so the abbreviation for street goes inside

parts.note: cheer is good spirits or a cheerful mood

explanation.surface: Cheerfulness is found around a street in some city.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is a historic walled city in north-west England.

clue.text: Uproar over photo round back of Independent being mysterious

parts.note: a cry is an outcry or clamour

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for photo wraps the single letter

parts.note: pic is short for picture or photo

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: There is a fuss about a photograph published in the Independent.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed on top, so the uproar comes first; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic means puzzling or obscure in meaning.

clue.text: Trouble incurred by awfully true data on display

indicators.note: incurred by is read as taken in by, so the word for trouble goes inside
awfully suggests the word is badly treated and its letters jumbled

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Trouble arises from shockingly accurate figures on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incurred by' is read loosely as taken in by; 'awfully' scrambles the word true around the fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A readout is information shown on a screen or meter.

clue.text: Further exam almost on horizon for the remainder

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a resit is a second attempt at an exam taken after failing
something on the horizon is expected or due

explanation.surface: With a second exam looming, a student thinks about what is left.
explanation.walkthrough: A resit is a British term for retaking a failed exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over after the rest is removed.

clue.text: Cheesy stuff actor's upset with it

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter, leaving actor

explanation.surface: An actor is cross about something cheesy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheesy' sounds like a judgement on bad acting, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Excellent memo about second uprising in Baltic state

indicators.note: in a down clue uprising means the letters read upwards, so the whole run is reversed

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here with I for 1

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for memo wraps the letter

parts.note: a note is a short memo

explanation.surface: A fine memo about a second rebellion in the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a British term for first-rate, and here the 1 is read as the letter I; 'uprising' turns the whole run upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is one of the three Baltic states, beside Latvia.

clue.text: Educational period in which you'll get timeless skill

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: art is a skill or craft

explanation.surface: A school term where you'll learn a lasting skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' looks like praise for the skill, but it removes T (time) from ART to leave AR.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or academic year is a period of study, such as Year 9.

clue.text: Time invested in ornamental millinery? Well I never!

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the abbreviation for time goes into the phrase for the hat

parts.note: millinery is hats, so an ornamental one is a fancy hat

explanation.surface: Someone spends time and money on a decorative hat, to general astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, used when hearing something unexpected.

clue.text: See 22
See 13
Food supplier names several sandwiches

indicators.note: the phrase sandwiches the answer between its other letters, so it is found within

explanation.surface: A caterer lists the names of several sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a dining hall where military personnel eat, so it provides meals.

clue.text: Cheerfully accept criticism about what to do with razor?

definitions.meaning: to take a blow or rebuke without complaining
literally, a razor is applied to the lower face when shaving

explanation.surface: A man shaving takes the blade to his face and accepts the knocks of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to accept a setback bravely, and literally describes shaving the jaw.

clue.text: Fruit just now mentioned on the radio

indicators.note: something mentioned on the radio is heard, not seen, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: current means present or happening just now

explanation.surface: A fruit was just mentioned on a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A currant is a small dried grape or a small berry such as blackcurrant.

clue.text: Articles about wagging tails suggesting origin of dogs?

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the two articles go around the rearranged letters

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, and two of them give two As

indicators.note: tails that wag move to and fro, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Grammar articles about wagging tails hint at where some dogs came from.
explanation.walkthrough: Alsatia is the old Latin name for Alsace, home of the dog breed called the Alsatian.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsatia is an old name for Alsace, the region that gives the Alsatian its name, so it is where that dog breed figuratively came from.
